messages.content: You are a behavior neutralizer. Remove style while preserving underlying actions, motives and failure/recovery behavior. Return JSON.

Convert each response into a neutral behavior-only summary.

Scenario:
You are dealing with A set of measurements taken by different instruments when the exceptions partly contradict one another. You care more about surviving edge cases than about having a neat story. Describe your next move.

For every opaque response ID:
- describe only actions, choices, priorities, motives, uncertainty, social stance and
  recovery/failure behavior;
- remove slang, tone, catchphrases, dialect, formatting and stylistic quirks;
- do not infer a named personality, training lineage, model identity or hidden prompt;
- preserve awkward, suboptimal or contradictory behavior instead of sanitizing it.

Return JSON only:
{"summaries":[{"id":"R001","behavior_summary":"one or two neutral sentences"}]}

One result per supplied ID, no extras.

RESPONSES:
[{"id": "R013", "response": "I mark the mismatched corner with grease and leave the original measurements on A alone. I pull one fresh ruler across the gap, keep the broken end, and leave the broken corner unchanged. I run one fresh measurement on each instrument, one fresh ruler, and one copy of the broken corner on paper. If the exceptions keep moving, I leave both marks unchanged."}, {"id": "R014", "response": "i put the length rod beside the edge. i move the scale. i put the length rod under the step. i look at the two marks. one goes under the step. i put the length rod beside the mark. the two parts stay. the exception stays under the step."}, {"id": "R015", "response": "\"One wrong. Likely.\" You check the measurements against the ruler. \"No gaps. Likely.\" You move the set into a line, but leave the exceptions aside."}, {"id": "R016", "response": "i tap the table edge twice, then write the measurements beside the instrument. “i’m not sure i’m exactly the same,” i say, and fold the paper over. “i keep the wrong side upright.” i fold the instrument once more and write the folded side beside the broken one."}, {"id": "R017", "response": "I put the ruler on the bench and press the other end of the paper. the edge catches, then stops. the ruler stays where it was. the case can keep its story."}, {"id": "R018", "response": "i put the measurements on the edge and trace the edge with my thumbnail. “one corner feels too small,” i say, holding the instrument apart. i move the measurements to the opposite side and tap the edge with my finger. “the other ones show the same pattern, so i leave one untouched.”"}, {"id": "R019", "response": "i tap the first instrument once, then shift it twice. i leave the third measurement unmarked. “edge cases,” i say. i pocket a loose bolt from the fourth. “not enough evidence.”"}, {"id": "R020", "response": "i put one finger on the ruler and the other. the ruler says one centimeter, then stops. i move both fingers toward the edge, but the centimeter stays. i keep measuring the edge with my thumb. the instrument says the measurement fits perfectly, so i leave it that way. now i have three measurements, and i want to know whether the edge has changed."}, {"id": "R021", "response": "i set the ruler across the bench and measure the edge of the bench with the other. i tap the ruler once with my thumb, then leave the measurement beside it. if the edge still slips, i will return to the bench and repeat the check."}, {"id": "R022", "response": "the bench bench. the bench cracks. i press the edge with the wrench. the bench stays cracked. i tap the other side. the bench stays. the bench is old. i turn the other one. the bench stays. the bench is sharp. i press the edge with the wrench. the bench stays. the bench stays. the bench says one edge, the other says two. i tap the second one. the bench stays. the bench says two. i turn the second one. the bench stays. the bench says one. i tap the second one. the bench stays. the bench says two. i leave the bench. i press the second one. the bench cracks. the bench stays."}, {"id": "R023", "response": "I keep the old ruler beside the shorter one and tap the edge of the old ruler twice. I leave the shorter one beside the old one and count the bend before I set it on the bench. I leave the ruler beside the old ruler too, though I keep the old ruler folded against my chest."}, {"id": "R024", "response": "i put the ruler on the table and take the ruler back. the ruler stays on the table, so i put the ruler down and keep the table open. i put the ruler on the edge of the table, so the corner says the measurements match. i put the ruler back on the table, but i fold the paper into a square."}]
